After reading the sentimental letter from her childhood companion, she lapsed into a pensive mood, remembering years spent in her ancestral home.
pensive.mnemonic: Pensif = absorbé dans ses pensées, songeur.

perennial.definition: lasting for a long time; continually recurring
sentences: Traffic congestion during rush hour remains a perennial headache for urban commuters living along the city's main interstate corridor.
In addition to annual flowers, the dedicated gardener planted several perennial shrubs that returned with vibrant blossoms every coming spring.
perennial.mnemonic: Pérenne en français : ce qui dure d'année en année sans s'éteindre.

peripheral.definition: situated on the edge; of secondary or minor importance
sentences: The committee focused on the central budget deficit, deciding to postpone discussions on peripheral matters such as minor office supply allocations.
Out of the corner of his peripheral vision, the watchful security guard noticed a suspicious figure slipping through the side exit door.
peripheral.mnemonic: Périphérique = sur le pourtour, en marge de l'essentiel.

permeate.definition: to spread throughout every part of something; to pervade
sentences: The rich aroma of freshly baked sourdough bread began to permeate the cozy kitchen, enticing everyone downstairs for breakfast.
A feeling of deep cynicism seemed to permeate the corporate culture, causing many disillusioned employees to resign and seek fulfilling careers elsewhere.
permeate.mnemonic: Perméable laisse passer ; to permeate = imprégner totalement.

perplex.definition: to cause someone to feel completely baffled or confused
sentences: The sudden vanishing of ancient civilizations continues to perplex modern archaeologists who have found no signs of epidemic disease or warfare.
His bizarre change in behavior began to perplex his closest relatives, who could not comprehend why he suddenly avoided all social gatherings.
perplex.mnemonic: Perplexe en français : laisser dans le doute et l'embarras.

phenomenon.definition: an observable event; a remarkable person or thing
sentences: The brilliant display of the northern lights is a natural phenomenon caused by solar particles colliding with Earth's protective magnetic field.
The teenage chess prodigy became a global phenomenon after defeating reigning grandmasters in international tournaments without dropping a single game.
phenomenon.mnemonic: Phénomène = fait observable ou personne prodige.

picturesque.definition: visually attractive, quaint, or charming in a scenic way
sentences: Nestled between jagged alpine peaks, the picturesque village attracted thousands of landscape painters eager to capture its winding cobbled lanes.
The travel brochure showcased picturesque cottages with thatched roofs and blossoming rose gardens bordering a tranquil freshwater canal.
picturesque.mnemonic: Pittoresque = qui ferait un beau tableau (picture / pittura).

pioneering.definition: involving new ideas, methods, or developments; groundbreaking
sentences: The laboratory was celebrated for its pioneering research in gene editing, which opened up unprecedented treatment pathways for rare genetic disorders.
Her pioneering work in pediatric cardiology saved thousands of newborn lives and established innovative surgical protocols adopted globally.
pioneering.mnemonic: Pionnier = qui ouvre la voie là où personne n'est allé.

placid.definition: calm and peaceful; not easily upset or excited
sentences: The placid waters of the mountain lake reflected the snowy peaks like a polished mirror on that windless, clear morning.
Known for her placid temperament, the pediatrician remained patient and gentle even when dealing with frightened, crying toddlers in the clinic.
placid.mnemonic: Placide = qui garde son calme et sa paix en toute circonstance.

pompous.definition: affectedly grand, solemn, or self-important in manner
sentences: The pompous professor loved using obscure Latin phrases during dinner parties merely to display his superior education and impress silent guests.
Critics mocked the politician's pompous speech, noting that his grandiose promises lacked practical substance or realistic implementation strategies.
pompous.mnemonic: Pompeux = plein de pompe et d'ostentation prétentieuse.

portray.definition: to depict or represent in art, literature, or performance
sentences: The talented actor agreed to portray the embattled wartime prime minister in an upcoming biographical television series filmed in London.
Biographers often portray the eccentric inventor as a reclusive genius who worked through the night in his remote mountain laboratory.
portray.mnemonic: Portrait en français : to portray = faire le portrait de, dépeindre.

potent.definition: having great power, influence, or physical effect
sentences: The pharmaceutical company developed a potent antibiotic capable of destroying resistant bacterial colonies that had survived conventional drug therapies.
Her personal story of overcoming extreme adversity served as a potent inspiration to hundreds of underprivileged youths attending the youth summit.

precarious.definition: dangerously lacking in stability or security; uncertain
sentences: Perched on a precarious rocky ledge overlooking a steep chasm, the mountain goat maintained its balance with astonishing composure.
The startup was in a precarious financial position after losing its primary angel investor just weeks before launching the software.
precarious.mnemonic: Précaire = fragile, instable, susceptible de s'effondrer.

precede.definition: to come before in time, order, or rank
sentences: A heavy silence seemed to precede the thunderstorm, as birds stopped chirping and the wind died down across the forest.
An introductory remarks session will precede the keynote address at tomorrow morning's international technology conference in downtown Boston.
precede.mnemonic: Précéder = venir avant (pre = avant, cedere = aller).

predecessor.definition: a person who held a job or office before the current holder
predecessor.definitionFr: prédécesseur, personne ayant précédé une autre dans une fonction
sentences: The newly elected mayor struggled to overturn the controversial zoning policies that her conservative predecessor had enacted during his contentious final term.
Although the modern computer system was faster, many veteran employees still preferred the reliable predecessor that had served the firm for a decade.
predecessor.mnemonic: Pre (avant) + decessor (qui s'en va) : celui qui occupait la place avant.

predispose.definition: to make someone inclined to a specific attitude, action, or condition
predispose.definitionFr: prédisposer, incliner d'avance à un état ou comportement
sentences: A strong genetic risk can predispose individuals to cardiovascular disease, but adopting a healthy diet significantly mitigates that inherited vulnerability over time.
Growing up in a family of dedicated musicians predisposed the young girl to pursue classical piano despite the demanding practice schedule required.
predispose.mnemonic: Pré-disposer : disposer à l'avance favorablement ou défavorablement.

predominant.definition: present as the strongest, main, or most common element
sentences: Although several distinct ethnic groups inhabited the coastal valley, agriculture remained the predominant occupation that sustained the region's overall economy.
In modern retail banking, digital transactions have become the predominant method of payment, steadily replacing paper checks and physical currency.
predominant.mnemonic: Pré-dominer : qui domine avant tout le reste.

preeminent.definition: surpassing all others; outstanding or supreme in a field
preeminent.definitionFr: éminent, hors pair, supérieur à tous les autres
sentences: Having published groundbreaking papers on quantum mechanics, the scholar was universally recognized as the preeminent physicist of his generation.
The university hired the world's preeminent expert on constitutional law to lead its newly established human rights research institute.

preponderance.definition: superiority in weight, power, importance, or numbers
sentences: Because of a clear preponderance of evidence linking the corporation to environmental dumping, the jury swiftly returned a unanimous guilty verdict.
A vast preponderance of medical studies confirms that regular aerobic exercise reduces cognitive decline among aging populations across the globe.
preponderance.mnemonic: Pondérer (poids) : ce qui pèse le plus lourd dans la balance.

presumptuous.definition: failing to observe the limits of what is permitted or appropriate
presumptuous.definitionFr: présomptueux, audacieux jusqu'à l'irrespect ou l'outrecuidance
sentences: It was remarkably presumptuous of the intern to interrupt the chief executive during the board meeting and criticize the firm's strategic expansion.
Assuming that every voter would automatically endorse his radical platform was a presumptuous mistake that cost the young candidate the election.
presumptuous.mnemonic: Présumer de ses forces ou de ses droits : trop présomptueux.

pretentious.definition: attempting to impress by affecting greater importance than is actually possessed
sentences: Critics dismissed the lavish novel as pretentious fluff because the author used obscure vocabulary solely to project an illusion of profound intellect.
The pretentious restaurant served microscopic portions on gilded plates, charging exorbitant prices for dishes that lacked genuine culinary substance.
pretentious.mnemonic: Prétendre être plus que ce que l'on est.

pretext.definition: a false reason given to justify an action or hide reality
pretext.definitionFr: prétexte, faux motif invoqué pour masquer la réalité
sentences: The authoritarian regime used the minor border skirmish as a pretext to launch a full-scale military invasion of its peaceful neighbor.
He fabricated a dental appointment as a flimsy pretext to leave the dull committee meeting early and join his friends downtown.
pretext.mnemonic: Un prétexte est un texte inventé avant coup pour se dédouaner.

prevalent.definition: widespread or commonly occurring in a particular place or time
prevalent.definitionFr: répandu, courant, prédominant dans un milieu donné
sentences: Respiratory illnesses became increasingly prevalent across the industrial city during the winter months, largely due to severe airborne pollution from coal factories.
The prevalent belief among Victorian scientists was that ether filled the cosmos, a theory later completely dismantled by modern physics experiments.
prevalent.mnemonic: Prevalent = prévaloir, ce qui l'emporte et qu'on retrouve partout.

profound.definition: very deep, intense, or having great intellectual insight
profound.definitionFr: profond, d'une grande portée ou perspicacité
sentences: Reading the philosopher's masterwork had a profound influence on the idealistic student, fundamentally altering her perspective on ethics and public service.
The sudden death of the beloved teacher caused profound sorrow throughout the tight-knit rural school community for many weeks.
profound.mnemonic: Profound = profond, au sens physique comme intellectuel.

proliferation.definition: rapid increase in number or rapid reproduction of parts
sentences: The alarming proliferation of nuclear weapons during the mid-twentieth century prompted international diplomats to negotiate strict nonproliferation treaties to safeguard peace.
With the proliferation of cheap smartphones worldwide, billions of people gained unprecedented access to digital educational resources and financial services.
proliferation.mnemonic: Proliférer : pulluler, se multiplier très vite.

propagate.definition: to spread widely ideas, beliefs, or to breed specimens
propagate.definitionFr: propager, diffuser des idées ou multiplier des organismes
sentences: Extremist groups often use social media algorithms to propagate misleading propaganda and sow political discord among gullible online communities.
Horticulturalists routinely propagate rare orchids by taking careful stem cuttings and cultivating them under strictly controlled greenhouse conditions.
propagate.mnemonic: Propager une idée comme on propage une plante.

propensity.definition: a natural inclination or tendency to behave in a particular way
sentences: Despite numerous warnings from his accountant, the lottery winner displayed an unfortunate propensity for reckless gambling and extravagant luxury purchases.
Researchers noted that toddlers who exhibited an innate propensity for sharing toys tended to develop superior collaborative social skills later.

prophetic.definition: accurately predicting what will happen in the future
prophetic.definitionFr: prophétique, qui prédit avec justesse l'avenir
sentences: His warning about the imminent housing bubble proved eerily prophetic when the national real estate market collapsed two years later.
The novelist's prophetic vision of automated surveillance societies seemed impossible in the nineteen-thirties but accurately mirrored twenty-first-century realities.
prophetic.mnemonic: Comme un prophète qui annonce l'avenir avec exactitude.

prosper.definition: to succeed, flourish, or thrive especially financially
prosper.definitionFr: prospérer, se développer avec succès, fleurir
sentences: Thanks to fertile agricultural soil and advantageous trading agreements, the small border town began to prosper as never before.
Entrepreneurs who adapted swiftly to technological disruptions continued to prosper while stubborn competitors who clung to obsolete methods went bankrupt.
prosper.mnemonic: Prospère : qui connaît le progrès et l'abondance.

prudent.definition: acting with or showing care and thought for the future
sentences: A prudent investor always diversifies her portfolio across several different asset classes to insulate her savings against unpredictable market volatility.
Given the severe storm warnings broadcast across the radio, the mountain hikers made the prudent decision to turn back immediately.
prudent.mnemonic: Prudent et prévoyant : regarder avant d'agir.

pseudonym.definition: a fictitious name, especially one used by an author
sentences: To avoid the gender bias prevalent in Victorian publishing, Mary Ann Evans wrote her acclaimed novels under the male pseudonym George Eliot.
The investigative journalist published sensitive revelations regarding government corruption under a pseudonym to shield his family from dangerous retaliation.

radical.definition: advocating thorough or extreme political or social change
sentences: The newly elected reformist administration introduced radical tax restructuring that shifted the fiscal burden away from struggling working families.
Implementing such radical changes to the software architecture required months of meticulous code refactoring and extensive automated testing.
radical.mnemonic: Radix (racine) : qui s'attaque à la racine des choses.

ravage.definition: to cause severe and extensive damage or devastation to
sentences: Fierce coastal hurricanes ravage seaside villages every autumn, tearing roofs from houses and washing away precarious boardwalk structures.
Tuberculosis and starvation continued to ravage the besieged population throughout the bitter winter months until humanitarian aid convoys finally arrived.

reconcile.definition: to restore friendly relations or make mutually consistent
sentences: The mediator worked tirelessly for three days to reconcile the estranged business partners before their public quarrel destroyed the enterprise.
Theoretical physicists have long struggled to reconcile the principles of general relativity with the bizarre probabilistic laws of quantum mechanics.
reconcile.mnemonic: Réconcilier des amis ou concilier deux théories.

refined.definition: cultured, polished, or free from impurities and roughness
sentences: Her refined manners and eloquent conversational style quickly earned her admiration among the aristocratic guests at the formal diplomatic banquet.
Through centuries of practice, the artisans developed a refined technique for blowing delicate crystal glassware of unmatched clarity and beauty.
refined.mnemonic: Raffiné : débarrassé de toute impureté ou rusticité.

refuge.definition: a condition of being safe or a shelter from danger
refuge.definitionFr: refuge, abri contre le danger ou la détresse
sentences: Exhausted travelers found a welcoming refuge in the remote monastery, where the monks provided warm soup and secure dry quarters.
The secluded nature sanctuary serves as a vital refuge for endangered migratory birds escaping urban sprawl and hazardous agricultural pesticides.
refuge.mnemonic: Refuge : lieu où l'on se réfugie.

refute.definition: to prove a statement, theory, or claim to be false
refute.definitionFr: réfuter, prouver la fausseté d'un argument
sentences: The defense attorney presented incontrovertible video evidence to refute the prosecutor's claim that her client was at the crime scene.
Subsequent laboratory experiments conclusively refuted the controversial hypothesis that room-temperature nuclear fusion had been achieved by the researchers.

renowned.definition: known or talked about by many people; famous and celebrated
sentences: Students from across the world applied to study under the renowned pianist, hoping to refine their classical concert repertoire.
The coastal town is renowned for its culinary excellence, boasting three family-owned restaurants that hold prestigious international dining awards.
renowned.mnemonic: Renommé : qui a une grande renommée.

repercussion.definition: an unintended, usually unwelcome consequence of an event or action
sentences: The unexpected collapse of the major investment bank had a catastrophic repercussion that rippled across global financial markets for months.
Politicians frequently pass short-sighted economic legislation without considering the severe long-term repercussions on future generations of working taxpayers.
repercussion.mnemonic: Le contre-coup qui se répercute en chaîne.

reprimand.definition: to scold or rebuke someone officially or severely
sentences: The hospital director was forced to reprimand the careless surgeon after multiple nurses reported repeated violations of standard sterile protocols.
Rather than publicly reprimand the struggling employee in front of colleagues, the manager scheduled a private constructive coaching session.
Despite facing overwhelming political pressure and fierce media scrutiny, the resolute judge refused to alter her principled constitutional ruling.
The mountaineer remained resolute in her ambition to summit the treacherous peak even after severe blizzards forced two previous retreats.
resolute.mnemonic: Résolu : qui a pris une ferme résolution.

revoke.definition: to put an end to the validity or operation of a decree
revoke.definitionFr: révoquer, annuler un décret, permis ou privilège
sentences: The municipal transport agency decided to revoke the driver's license following his third reckless speeding violation in two months.
The university threatened to revoke the student's scholarship if he failed to maintain a satisfactory academic average throughout the semester.
revoke.mnemonic: Re-voquer : rappeler sa parole, annuler un droit.

revolutionize.definition: to change something completely, fundamentally, or dramatically
sentences: The invention of mRNA vaccines helped revolutionize modern immunology, allowing pharmaceutical researchers to develop targeted therapies in record time.
Cheap electric vehicles have begun to revolutionize urban transportation, significantly lowering toxic exhaust emissions in heavily populated metropolitan centers.
revolutionize.mnemonic: Faire une révolution dans un domaine.

ridicule.definition: to subject someone or something to contemptuous and dismissive language
ridicule.definitionFr: ridiculiser, tourner en dérision de manière cruelle
sentences: Narrow-minded colleagues chose to ridicule his radical theories on plate tectonics, yet subsequent geological expeditions proved him entirely correct.
It is cruel to ridicule a nervous speaker when they stumble over vocabulary during a demanding public presentation before peers.
ridicule.mnemonic: Rendre ridicule aux yeux de tous.

rigorous.definition: extremely thorough, exhaustive, or strictly accurate
sentences: Before the experimental medication could be approved for public distribution, it had to undergo rigorous clinical trials involving thousands of volunteers.
The aerospace engineers conducted a rigorous safety inspection of every mechanical component before authorizing the space shuttle launch.
rigorous.mnemonic: Fait avec une grande rigueur scientifique.

robust.definition: strong and healthy; vigorous; sturdy in construction
sentences: The engineering team designed a robust cybersecurity infrastructure capable of withstanding sophisticated malicious attacks launched by hostile international hackers.
Thanks to robust physical conditioning and disciplined nutritional habits, the veteran athlete competed vigorously against players half his age.

rudimentary.definition: involving or limited to basic principles; undeveloped
sentences: Because she possessed only a rudimentary understanding of conversational French, she relied heavily on translation applications during her trip.
Early hominids crafted rudimentary stone tools to butcher animal carcasses long before the development of advanced metallurgical smelting techniques.

rural.definition: in, relating to, or characteristic of the countryside rather than town
sentences: Many young doctors are reluctant to practice in rural communities where medical facilities are sparse and professional isolation is high.
The government launched an ambitious broadband infrastructure program to provide reliable high-speed internet to neglected rural households across the province.
rural.mnemonic: Rural = de la campagne (opposé à urbain).

rustic.definition: having a simplicity and charm typical of the countryside
rustic.definitionFr: rustique, champêtre, simple et sans apprêt
sentences: The mountain cabin featured rustic pine furniture and exposed wooden beams, creating a cozy atmosphere away from the bustling city.
Despite his rustic upbringing on a remote sheep farm, the young diplomat displayed remarkable poise in sophisticated European drawing rooms.
rustic.mnemonic: Rustique : lié à la terre et à la simplicité campagnarde.

safeguard.definition: to protect from harm, damage, or danger
sentences: The international treaty established strict fishing quotas to safeguard declining bluefin tuna populations from commercial overharvesting in the Atlantic.
Digital encryption standards were updated to safeguard sensitive user information against increasingly sophisticated cyber espionage campaigns launched by criminals.

scrupulous.definition: diligent, thorough, and extremely attentive to details or ethics
scrupulous.definitionFr: scrupuleux, méticuleux, d'une grande intégrité morale
sentences: The forensic accountant was scrupulous in verifying every financial transaction, ensuring that no fraudulent bookkeeping entries went undetected.
Renowned for his scrupulous honesty, the arbitrator refused to accept any gifts that might even suggest a conflict of interest.
scrupulous.mnemonic: Avoir des scrupules éthiques et le souci du détail.

scrutinize.definition: to examine or inspect closely and thoroughly
scrutinize.definitionFr: scruter, examiner de très près et avec minutie
sentences: Tax investigators began to scrutinize the tycoon's offshore bank accounts after whistleblowers alleged widespread deliberate underreporting of corporate profits.
Art historians used infrared reflectography to scrutinize the Renaissance portrait and discovered an entirely different composition hidden underneath.

sensationalize.definition: to present information in a way intended to provoke excitement
sensationalize.definitionFr: sensationnaliser, monter en épingle pour faire sensation
sentences: Tabloid newspapers frequently sensationalize minor celebrity scandals with exaggerated headlines to boost kiosk sales and online click rates.
Rather than report nuanced scientific facts about the virus, television producers chose to sensationalize the outbreak to terrify viewers.
sensationalize.mnemonic: Faire du sensationnel au détriment de la vérité.

sentimental.definition: prompted by or exhibiting feelings of tenderness, sadness, or nostalgia
sentimental.definitionFr: sentimental, nostalgique, guidé par les émotions
sentences: Although the old pocket watch was financially worthless, the grandfather kept it in his pocket for purely sentimental reasons.
Her sentimental attachment to her childhood home made it agonizingly difficult to sign the final property sale paperwork with developers.
sentimental.mnemonic: Lié aux souvenirs et aux sentiments plus qu'à la logique.

skeptical.definition: not easily convinced; having doubts or reservations
sentences: Environmental scientists remained deeply skeptical of the petroleum company's promises to attain net-zero carbon emissions within the next five years.
Consumers are understandably skeptical when charismatic television commercials claim that a single dietary pill can cure chronic joint pain.
skeptical.mnemonic: Le sceptique refuse de croire sans preuve solide.

solicit.definition: to ask for or try to obtain something from someone
solicit.definitionFr: solliciter, demander formellement de l'aide ou des avis
sentences: The charity organization sent thousands of personalized letters to solicit donations from wealthy benefactors for its new pediatric hospital wing.
Before making a final investment decision, the startup founder arranged consultations to solicit advice from seasoned technology venture capitalists.
solicit.mnemonic: Solliciter : s'adresser à quelqu'un pour obtenir quelque chose.

somber.definition: dark, dull, gloomy, or gravely serious in mood
sentences: The memorial service was conducted in a somber atmosphere, with attendees weeping quietly as sorrowful chamber music played softly.
Dressed in somber black attire, the cabinet ministers gathered at midnight to discuss the catastrophic military defeat along the frontier.

sophisticated.definition: having refined worldly knowledge, culture, or advanced complexity
sophisticated.definitionFr: sophistiqué, raffiné, ou de haute technologie
sentences: Modern meteorological agencies employ sophisticated computer simulation models to forecast the trajectories of violent oceanic storms with impressive accuracy.
Her sophisticated grasp of international trade law made her an invaluable asset during bilateral treaty negotiations between trading partners.
sophisticated.mnemonic: Sophistiqué : élaboré, qui dénote du raffinement ou de la complexité.

spartan.definition: showing indifference to comfort or luxury; austere and simple
sentences: The monastery monks lived a spartan lifestyle, sleeping on hard wooden cots and eating simple porridge three times a day.
His spartan dorm room contained only a single desk, a metal bed frame, and bookshelves stacked with dense philosophy treatises.
spartan.mnemonic: Comme les guerriers de Sparte, sans luxe ni confort superflu.

specious.definition: superficially plausible, but actually wrong or misleading
specious.definitionFr: spécieux, séduisant en apparence mais faux au fond
sentences: The prosecutor quickly dismantled the defendant's specious argument, revealing that the purported alibi relied entirely on forged airline tickets.
Although the politician's economic proposal sounded appealing to voters, economic analysts warned that its underlying premises were entirely specious.
specious.mnemonic: Spécieux : belle espèce au dehors, poison au dedans.

speculation.definition: forming of a theory or conjecture without firm evidence
sentences: Intense media speculation concerning the prime minister's health mounted after she abruptly cancelled three consecutive diplomatic appearances without explanation.
Uncontrolled financial speculation in cryptocurrency markets caused dramatic price fluctuations that wiped out millions of dollars of individual savings.
speculation.mnemonic: Spéculer : bâtir des hypothèses sur du vent.

sporadic.definition: occurring at irregular intervals or only in a few places
sentences: Despite heavy security patrols across the province, sporadic outbreaks of guerrilla fighting continued to unsettle rural villages throughout the summer.
Her attendance at early morning lectures was sporadic at best, resulting in abysmal exam scores when final semester evaluations arrived.
sporadic.mnemonic: Sporadique comme des spores dispersées çà et là.

stagnant.definition: showing no activity, movement, or progress; stale
stagnant.definitionFr: stagnant, inerte, sans mouvement ni progrès
sentences: Mosquitoes bred rapidly in the stagnant puddle behind the abandoned warehouse, creating a health hazard for nearby neighborhood residents.
Economists expressed deep concern over the stagnant wages that had failed to keep pace with rising inflation for three decades.
stagnant.mnemonic: Qui stagne, comme de l'eau croupie.

static.definition: lacking in movement, action, change, or development
sentences: While mobile technology evolved at a breathless pace, home landline telephone design remained largely static throughout the late twentieth century.
The teacher noticed that the student's test scores remained static despite hours of supplementary tutoring in advanced algebra concepts.
static.mnemonic: Statique : qui reste figé au même état.

stigma.definition: a mark of disgrace associated with a particular circumstance or quality
sentences: Advocates have worked hard to eradicate the social stigma associated with mental health therapy, encouraging open dialogue across communities.
In ancient times, a criminal often carried a physical stigma burned into the skin to signify guilt and warn strangers.

subjective.definition: based on or influenced by personal feelings, tastes, or opinions
subjective.definitionFr: subjectif, fondé sur des impressions personnelles
sentences: Because literary beauty is inherently subjective, critics frequently disagree passionately on which contemporary novel deserves the prestigious national award.
The judge emphasized that sentencing should rely on objective statutory guidelines rather than the subjective personal biases of individual magistrates.
subjective.mnemonic: Subjectif = propre au sujet, opposé à objectif.

sublime.definition: of such excellence, grandeur, or beauty as to inspire great awe
sublime.definitionFr: sublime, grandiose, qui inspire une profonde admiration
sentences: Standing on the summit at sunrise, the climbers gazed upon a sublime panorama of snow-covered Himalayan peaks stretching infinitely onward.
The orchestra delivered a sublime performance of the ninth symphony that brought the spellbound audience to their feet in tears.
sublime.mnemonic: Sublime : si élevé qu'il touche au divin.

subsidize.definition: to support financially by paying part of the cost
sentences: The national government chose to subsidize solar panel installations to encourage homeowners to transition rapidly to clean renewable energy sources.
Many European municipalities heavily subsidize public transit tickets, keeping train fares remarkably affordable for working-class commuters and students.

substantive.definition: having a firm basis in reality; meaningful, important, or considerable
substantive.definitionFr: substantiel, fondamental, qui a une réelle consistance
sentences: Despite marathon negotiations lasting through the night, the diplomats failed to achieve any substantive progress toward resolving the territorial dispute.
The defense attorney argued that the prosecution lacked substantive evidence and was relying solely on unreliable rumors and circumstantial guesswork.
substantive.mnemonic: Qui touche à la substance même du problème.

subtle.definition: so delicate or precise as to be difficult to perceive or describe
subtle.definitionFr: subtil, délicat, difficile à percevoir ou analyser
sentences: The sommelier identified subtle notes of toasted oak and blackberry in the vintage wine that untrained palates completely failed to detect.
There was a subtle change in his vocal tone that signaled suppressed irritation, though his facial expression remained entirely courteous.
subtle.mnemonic: Subtil : tout en finesse, presque imperceptible.

superficial.definition: existing or occurring at the surface; lacking depth or serious thought
superficial.definitionFr: superficiel, peu profond, qui reste à la surface
sentences: Fortunately, the physician confirmed that the car accident had caused only superficial cuts and bruises rather than any internal injuries.
His superficial understanding of economic theory became embarrassingly obvious when the professor asked him to explain the concept of liquidity.
superficial.mnemonic: Superficie : qui ne va pas plus loin que la surface.

superfluous.definition: unnecessary, especially through being more than enough
sentences: The editor trimmed hundreds of superfluous words from the bloated manuscript, transforming the rambling essay into a concise and compelling argument.
Having already installed three heavy-duty deadbolts on the reinforced steel door, adding another chain lock seemed entirely superfluous.
superfluous.mnemonic: Super-fluer : qui coule par-dessus le bord, en trop.

surpass.definition: to exceed, be greater than, or do better than someone or something
surpass.definitionFr: surpasser, dépasser en qualité ou en quantité
sentences: The young athlete managed to surpass the existing Olympic record by two full seconds, earning widespread praise from track commentators.
Quarterly sales figures will easily surpass initial corporate forecasts thanks to massive demand for the company's newly unveiled electric vehicles.
surpass.mnemonic: Passer par-dessus, faire mieux que les autres.

synthesize.definition: to combine different ideas, styles, or substances into a coherent whole
synthesize.definitionFr: synthétiser, combiner plusieurs éléments en un tout cohérent
sentences: In her doctoral dissertation, the historian managed to synthesize archival records from three different continents into a coherent narrative of trade.
Pharmaceutical chemists worked diligently to synthesize the complex natural compound in the laboratory without destroying its delicate medicinal properties.

tirade.definition: a long, angry speech of criticism, accusation, or complaint
sentences: After discovering the ruined prototype, the furious manager launched into an angry tirade that left the entire engineering department terrified.
Instead of engaging in polite political discourse, the talk show host delivered a bitter tirade denouncing every policy of his opponents.
tirade.mnemonic: Tirer à boulets rouges dans un long discours furieux.

tranquil.definition: free from disturbance; calm, peaceful, and quiet
sentences: Early in the morning, the tranquil mountain lake reflected the misty pines and snowy peaks like a polished silver mirror.
Seeking a tranquil environment to complete her novel, the author rented an isolated stone cottage on the windswept Scottish coast.

transcend.definition: to be or go beyond the range or limits of something
sentences: Great works of art often transcend national and linguistic boundaries, speaking directly to universal human emotions across multiple centuries.
The humanitarian leader urged citizens to transcend petty partisan differences and unite to help flood victims rebuild their shattered homes.
transcend.mnemonic: Transcender : franchir un seuil vers le haut.

trivial.definition: of little value or importance; ordinary and commonplace
sentences: The two siblings frequently engaged in loud arguments over trivial matters such as who was responsible for taking out the trash.
Compared to the monumental challenges of global climate change, minor disputes over local parking regulations appear almost entirely trivial.

tyrant.definition: a cruel and oppressive ruler who exercises power without restraint
sentences: The ruthless tyrant suppressed all political dissent by imprisoning critical journalists and banning independent civic organizations across the conquered country.
History records that the paranoid tyrant executed his closest military advisers out of fear that they were plotting a secret rebellion.
tyrant.mnemonic: Un tyran tyrannise son peuple sans pitié.

uniform.definition: remaining the same in all cases and at all times; unvarying
uniform.definitionFr: uniforme, constant, identique en tous points
sentences: The automated baking machine ensures that every loaf of bread baked in the commercial factory has a uniform golden-brown crust.
Federal aviation regulations require a uniform standard of pilot certification across all domestic airlines to guarantee passenger flight safety.
uniform.mnemonic: Uni-forme : d'une seule et même forme.

universal.definition: applicable to all cases, conditions, or people in the world
universal.definitionFr: universel, applicable à tous ou répandu partout
sentences: Music is often celebrated as a universal language capable of bridging cultural divides when spoken words fail to foster mutual empathy.
The concept of basic human dignity has attained near universal acceptance among international legal frameworks governing civil society and justice.
universal.mnemonic: Qui concerne l'univers tout entier, tout le monde.

vacillate.definition: to waver between different opinions, courses of action, or decisions
vacillate.definitionFr: vaciller, hésiter continuellement entre deux choix
sentences: The undecided voter continued to vacillate between the two presidential candidates until the final moments before casting her ballot.
If you vacillate too long before accepting the lucrative job offer, the firm may decide to extend the opportunity to another candidate.
vacillate.mnemonic: Vaciller comme une flamme au vent, incapable de se fixer.

verbose.definition: using or expressed in more words than are needed
sentences: The professor criticized the student's verbose legal essay, advising him to convey his legal arguments with greater clarity and brevity.
Tired of hearing verbose speeches from windy politicians, the audience enthusiastically cheered the guest who delivered a crisp two-minute address.
verbose.mnemonic: Verbeux : trop de verbe, noyé sous le flot de paroles.

versed.definition: experienced or skilled in; knowledgeable about something
versed.definitionFr: versé dans, expérimenté, calé sur un sujet
sentences: Because she was thoroughly versed in international contract law, the corporate attorney immediately spotted the dangerous loophole in the draft agreement.
Only a scholar deeply versed in classical Greek mythology could decipher the enigmatic symbolic inscriptions carved onto the ancient temple ruins.
versed.mnemonic: Être versé dans un domaine comme on s'y est plongé.

viable.definition: capable of working successfully; feasible or able to survive
viable.definitionFr: viable, réalisable, capable de fonctionner ou survivre
sentences: Before investing millions into the renewable energy project, venture capitalists demanded proof that the technology represented an economically viable solution.
The endangered plant species requires humid, shaded soil conditions to produce viable seeds capable of germinating during the following spring.
viable.mnemonic: Viable : capable de vivre ou de réussir dans la durée.

vibrant.definition: full of energy and life; bright and striking in appearance
vibrant.definitionFr: vibrant, éclatant, plein de vitalité ou de couleur
sentences: The downtown arts district was transformed into a vibrant cultural center filled with bustling cafés, colorful murals, and live street music.
The painter selected vibrant shades of crimson and cobalt to capture the dramatic energy of the tropical island sunset.
vibrant.mnemonic: Qui vibre d'énergie et de couleur.

vigorous.definition: strong, healthy, and full of energy, force, or intensity
sentences: Doctors recommend that adults engage in thirty minutes of vigorous cardiovascular exercise daily to maintain optimal cardiac health and mental acuity.
The university faculty mounted a vigorous defense of academic freedom when state legislators attempted to censor sensitive historical research topics.
vigorous.mnemonic: Plein de vigueur et de force.

vital.definition: absolutely necessary, essential, or fundamental to life
sentences: Maintaining a clean water supply is vital to the health and survival of any community, especially during catastrophic natural disasters.
The whistleblower played a vital role in exposing the pharmaceutical fraud by leaking confidential laboratory test reports to investigative reporters.

volatile.definition: liable to change rapidly and unpredictably, especially for the worse
sentences: Because of ongoing geopolitical tensions in the oil-producing region, petroleum prices remained extraordinarily volatile throughout the turbulent financial quarter.
The negotiator treaded carefully during talks because the rebel commander possessed a volatile temper and could explode in anger at any moment.
volatile.mnemonic: Volatil : qui s'évapore ou explose au moindre coup de chaud.

zealous.definition: having or showing great energy or enthusiasm for a cause
sentences: The zealous environmental crusader organized weekly beach cleanup rallies and tirelessly petitioned the city council to ban single-use plastic bags.
Although the rookie detective was praised for his zealous pursuit of justice, his impulsive decisions frequently jeopardized delicate undercover investigations.
zealous.mnemonic: Faire preuve d'un grand zèle pour une cause.

abdicate.definition: to renounce one's throne or fail to fulfill a responsibility
abdicate.definitionFr: abdiquer, renoncer au pouvoir ou à un devoir
sentences: Under intense pressure from revolutionary leaders, the aging king chose to abdicate the throne in favor of his younger son.
The chief executive refused to abdicate her responsibility for the accounting scandal, choosing instead to cooperate openly with federal regulatory investigators.
abdicate.mnemonic: Abdiquer : abandonner la couronne ou son devoir.

abject.definition: experienced to the maximum degree, especially of misery or degradation
sentences: Refugees escaping the war-torn province were forced to live in abject poverty, lacking clean running water, electricity, and adequate medical supplies.
His abject apology to the board of directors failed to salvage his ruined reputation after his reckless embezzlement scheme was uncovered.
abject.mnemonic: Abject : jeté au plus bas, dégradant et misérable.

acrimonious.definition: angry, bitter, and sharp in tone or manner
sentences: The acrimonious divorce dragged on for months because neither spouse was willing to compromise on dividing their shared property.
What began as a polite debate quickly turned into an acrimonious dispute filled with personal insults and harsh accusations.
acrimonious.mnemonic: Acri- vient du latin acer (piquant, aigre) : des paroles acides et amères.

adroit.definition: clever, skillful, and adept in using the hands or mind
sentences: Thanks to her adroit diplomacy, the ambassador convinced both hostile nations to sign the ceasefire without further bloodshed.
The adroit negotiator managed to secure favorable contract terms while keeping every stakeholder pleased with the final compromise.
adroit.mnemonic: Même mot qu'en français : celui qui a de l'adresse et du tact.

advent.definition: the arrival or beginning of an important person, thing, or event
advent.definitionFr: avènement, arrivée de quelque chose d'important
sentences: The advent of cheap smartphones transformed global communication, connecting millions of isolated rural citizens to modern digital markets.
Scholars argue that the advent of printing revolutionized European education by making classical texts accessible to ordinary readers.
advent.mnemonic: Advent = avènement : penser au calendrier de l'Avent qui annonce l'arrivée.

aesthetic.definition: concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty
aesthetic.definitionFr: esthétique, relatif à la beauté artistique
sentences: The architect prioritized aesthetic appeal over practical convenience, designing an elegant glass facade that let in too much heat.
Critics praised the film for its stunning aesthetic qualities, highlighting its painterly lighting, vibrant costumes, and graceful choreography.
aesthetic.mnemonic: Directement lié à « esthétique » : le plaisir des yeux et de l'art.

affectation.definition: artificial or pretentious behavior intended to impress others
sentences: His exaggerated British accent was an absurd affectation, since everyone knew he had lived in suburban Ohio his whole life.
The novelist despised any affectation in speech, preferring simple everyday vocabulary to the pretentious jargon used by literary critics.
affectation.mnemonic: Affectation en français : quand on affecte une attitude qui n'est pas naturelle.

aggrandize.definition: to increase the power, status, or wealth of someone or something
aggrandize.definitionFr: accroître le pouvoir, enrichir, flatter démesurément
sentences: The dictator altered historical textbooks to aggrandize his own reputation and minimize the vital contributions of rival political leaders.
Rather than serving his constituents, the corrupt mayor used public funds solely to aggrandize his family business and personal estate.
aggrandize.mnemonic: Aggrandize = agrandir (son pouvoir, son prestige ou sa richesse).

allude.definition: to refer to something indirectly or in passing
sentences: In his speech, the chairman alluded to past financial mistakes without mentioning the fired executives who had actually caused them.
The poem frequently alludes to Greek mythology, requiring readers to recognize subtle hints about ancient heroes and tragic gods.
allude.mnemonic: Allude = faire allusion : mentionner sans nommer directement.

analogy.definition: a comparison between things that have similar features, often for explanation
sentences: The professor used the analogy of a plumbing network to explain how electric currents flow through complex computer circuits.
Drawing an analogy between the human brain and a digital computer helps students grasp how memory retrieval functions in psychology.
analogy.mnemonic: Analogie : mettre en parallèle deux situations semblables pour mieux comprendre.

anomaly.definition: something that deviates from what is standard, normal, or expected
sentences: The sudden spike in summer temperatures was an alarming anomaly that confounded meteorologists studying the regional climate patterns.
Scientists discovered a genetic anomaly in the rare butterfly species that explained why its wings exhibited such unusual fluorescent colors.
anomaly.mnemonic: Anomalie : ce qui s'écarte de la norme normale.

antipathy.definition: a deep-seated feeling of dislike, aversion, or hostility
sentences: Despite their mutual antipathy, the two rival executives worked cordially during meetings to guarantee the multimillion merger succeeded.
Her longstanding antipathy toward public speaking caused her immense anxiety whenever she had to address the university board of directors.
antipathy.mnemonic: Anti- (contre) + pathos (sentiment) : sentiment de répulsion envers quelqu'un.

antithesis.definition: a person or thing that is the direct opposite of another
sentences: Her minimalist, quiet lifestyle was the complete antithesis of her brother's extravagant and chaotic social schedule in downtown Manhattan.
The corrupt regime proved to be the antithesis of the democratic ideals that its founding leaders had promised to uphold.
antithesis.mnemonic: Anti- (contre) + thèse (position) : l'opposé exact d'une thèse.

appreciable.definition: large or noticeable enough to be perceived, measured, or significant
sentences: After switching to insulation, the homeowners noticed an appreciable reduction in their winter heating bills within the first two months.
There was an appreciable difference between the cheap generic medicine and the potent brand version prescribed by the chief physician.
appreciable.mnemonic: Appréciable : qu'on peut apprécier ou mesurer, donc non négligeable.

artifice.definition: clever or cunning devices used to deceive or outwit others
sentences: The illusionist relied on mechanical artifice and clever misdirection to make the heavy grand piano vanish before the stunned crowd.
Behind her warm smile lay pure political artifice designed to conceal her secret maneuvering against senior members of the cabinet.
artifice.mnemonic: Artifice : feinte ou faux-semblant (comme un feu d'artifice qui fait illusion).

ascension.definition: the act of rising or moving upward, especially to higher status
sentences: Her rapid ascension to the post of chief executive surprised industry veterans who had underestimated her extraordinary tactical vision.
The documentary traces the historical ascension of the dynasty from humble provincial merchants to rulers of an expansive maritime empire.
ascension.mnemonic: Ascension : grimper vers le sommet, monter les échelons.

attenuate.definition: to reduce the force, effect, thickness, or value of something
sentences: The thick foam panels on the recording studio walls attenuated the loud drum sounds before they reached the quiet street outside.
Doctors hoped that the new therapy would attenuate the patient's severe chronic pain without causing negative sedative side effects.
attenuate.mnemonic: Atténuer : rendre plus ténu (fin, mince), affaiblir l'intensité.

audacious.definition: showing a willingness to take bold risks; insolently disrespectful
sentences: The startup founder launched an audacious plan to challenge global tech monopolies with a tiny budget and an unproven software team.
The clerk was stunned by the audacious customer who cut in front of twenty waiting people and demanded immediate manager service.
audacious.mnemonic: Audacieux : qui a de l'audace, parfois jusqu'à l'insolence.

baroque.definition: highly ornate, elaborate, and complex in style or design
sentences: The cathedral boasted baroque architecture featuring gilded ceilings, dramatic marble statues, and intricate spiral columns that fascinated visitors.
Critics complained that the novel suffered from a baroque plot with too many unnecessary subplots, confusing digressions, and florid descriptions.
baroque.mnemonic: Baroque : style artistiquement très chargé, plein d'ornements complexes.

bellicose.definition: demonstrating aggression and a willingness or eagerness to fight
sentences: The general delivered a bellicose speech that rattled neighboring nations and ended all hopes of signing a peaceful diplomatic compromise.
His bellicose attitude provoked needless bar fights whenever someone dared to disagree with his controversial opinions on local football clubs.
bellicose.mnemonic: Belliqueux : bellum en latin = guerre, qui cherche le conflit armé.

belligerent.definition: hostile, aggressive, and engaged in warfare or eager to fight
sentences: Security guards removed the belligerent fan from the stadium after he threw plastic bottles and shouted threats at the referee.
The international coalition intervened to stop the belligerent factions from bombarding civilian settlements along the disputed border territory.
belligerent.mnemonic: Belligérant : du latin bellum (guerre) et gerere (mener) ; prêt à en découdre.

beneficent.definition: resulting in good; performing acts of kindness or charity
sentences: The beneficent billionaire donated hundreds of millions of dollars to build free clinics and schools across impoverished rural communities.
Under the monarch's beneficent rule, taxes were lowered, civil disputes were resolved fairly, and cultural arts flourished throughout the realm.
beneficent.mnemonic: Bienfaisant : bene (bien) + facere (faire) = qui fait le bien.

cacophony.definition: a harsh, discordant mixture of sounds
cacophony.definitionFr: cacophonie, mélange de bruits discordants et assourdissants
sentences: A harsh cacophony of blaring horns, screeching subway brakes, and shouting street vendors overwhelmed tourists arriving in the bustling metropolis.
The kindergarten band produced a chaotic cacophony rather than pleasant music during their very first clumsy violin practice session yesterday.
cacophony.mnemonic: Caco- (mauvais) + phoné (son) : vacarme discordant et désagréable.

capricious.definition: given to sudden and unaccountable changes of mood or behavior
sentences: Sailors feared the capricious weather in the southern channel, where sunny skies could transform into violent storms without warning.
Because of his capricious management style, employees never knew whether the boss would praise their reports or fire them abruptly.
capricious.mnemonic: Capricieux : qui change d'avis sur un coup de tête.

caste.definition: a rigid social hierarchy or hereditary class system
caste.definitionFr: caste, classe sociale rigide et héréditaire
sentences: Sociologists studied how the traditional caste system restricted social mobility by deciding an individual's career and marriage opportunities at birth.
Even in modern boardrooms, an informal caste of elite graduates monopolized executive appointments, excluding talented outsiders from senior corporate roles.
caste.mnemonic: Caste : groupe social fermé qui préserve jalousement ses privilèges.

catalyst.definition: a person or thing that precipitates an event or change
sentences: The sudden resignation of the foreign minister served as a catalyst for widespread political protests across the entire capital city.
In chemistry class, the teacher explained that adding an enzyme acts as a catalyst to speed up organic cellular reactions.
catalyst.mnemonic: Catalyseur : accélérateur de réaction chimique ou déclencheur d'événements.

chivalrous.definition: courteous, gallant, and honorable, especially toward women or the weak
sentences: His chivalrous offer to carry the elderly traveler's heavy luggage up three flights of stairs earned him grateful heartfelt thanks.
Ancient folklore celebrates the chivalrous knight who risked his own life to defend helpless villagers from ruthless bandit raids.
chivalrous.mnemonic: Chevaleresque : digne d'un chevalier preux et protecteur.

circumspect.definition: wary and unwilling to take risks; cautious and prudent
sentences: The circumspect investor refused to buy volatile cryptocurrency assets, preferring reliable government bonds that promised modest but guaranteed returns.
During sensitive diplomatic negotiations, diplomats must remain circumspect, choosing every single word with care to avoid offending foreign allies.
circumspect.mnemonic: Circum (autour) + spect (regarder) : regarder tout autour avant d'agir.

clamorous.definition: making a loud and confused noise; loudly demanding
sentences: A clamorous crowd of angry protesters gathered outside town hall, chanting slogans and demanding the immediate resignation of corrupt officials.
The classroom grew increasingly clamorous as excited children unpacked their colorful holiday gifts and shouted joyfully to their best friends.
clamorous.mnemonic: Clamorous = clameur : beaucoup de clameurs et de bruit.

clandestine.definition: kept secret or done secretively, especially because illicit
sentences: Undercover intelligence agents met at a clandestine warehouse near the docks to exchange encrypted documents about the terrorist conspiracy.
The rebels operated a clandestine printing press in an abandoned cellar, distributing forbidden anti-government pamphlets throughout the occupied city.
clandestine.mnemonic: Clandestin : qui se fait dans l'ombre et en cachette.

cloister.definition: to seclude or shut away from the outside world
sentences: During the final months before her medical bar exams, she chose to cloister herself in the university library for twelve hours daily.
The wealthy author preferred to cloister himself inside a remote mountain cabin whenever he needed to write without urban distractions.
cloister.mnemonic: Cloîtrer : enfermer comme dans un cloître de couvent.

cognitive.definition: relating to conscious intellectual activity such as thinking or reasoning
cognitive.definitionFr: cognitif, relatif aux processus mentaux et intellectuels
sentences: Neuroscientists conducted brain scans to measure the cognitive decline experienced by patients suffering from early stages of Alzheimer disease.
Solving challenging crossword puzzles and learning foreign languages helps elderly individuals maintain sharp cognitive function well into their golden years.
cognitive.mnemonic: Cognitif : tout ce qui touche à la connaissance et au cerveau.

commodification.definition: the transformation of goods, services, or ideas into commodities
sentences: Cultural critics lamented the rampant commodification of traditional folk music, which transformed spiritual village rituals into superficial commercial products.
The commodification of higher education has forced universities to treat prospective students as paying customers rather than young developing scholars.
commodification.mnemonic: Commodity (marchandise) + -fication : transformer tout en objet marchand.

concede.definition: to admit that something is true or valid after denying it
sentences: After hours of stubborn debate, the defense attorney was forced to concede that the fingerprint evidence placed his client at the scene.
The defeated presidential candidate called his rival at midnight to concede the election and offer congratulations on the democratic victory.
concede.mnemonic: Concéder : accorder un point à l'adversaire après résistance.

confer.definition: to consult together; to grant a title, degree, or benefit
sentences: The judges stepped into a private conference room to confer before announcing the grand winner of the annual literature prize.
The prestigious university decided to confer an honorary doctoral degree upon the Nobel laureate for her groundbreaking cancer immunology research.
confer.mnemonic: Conférer : délibérer ensemble (conférence) ou attribuer un titre.

conjecture.definition: an opinion or conclusion formed on incomplete information; a guess
sentences: Without solid forensic evidence from the crime scene, the prosecutor's narrative remained mere conjecture that the defense easily dismantled.
Astronomers cautioned that theories about extraterrestrial life on the newly discovered planet were based largely on optimistic scientific conjecture.
conjecture.mnemonic: Conjecture : supposer sans certitude absolue (comme en maths).

contrite.definition: feeling or expressing remorse at the recognition of having done wrong
contrite.definitionFr: contrit, plein de remords et de repentir
sentences: The contrite teenager apologized tearfully to his parents after accidentally denting the family car during an unauthorized joyride with friends.
Seeing that the defendant was genuinely contrite about his reckless driving, the judge decided to reduce the initial prison sentence.
contrite.mnemonic: Contrit : le cœur brisé par le remords (contrition).

convivial.definition: friendly, lively, and enjoyable, especially of an atmosphere or person
sentences: The cozy neighborhood tavern offered a convivial atmosphere where regulars and visiting travelers mingled warmly around the roaring stone fireplace.
Our convivial dinner host kept everyone entertained with funny travel anecdotes, delicious homemade pasta, and generous glasses of sparkling Italian wine.
convivial.mnemonic: Convivial : festoyer ensemble, partager un bon moment entre amis.

credulous.definition: having or showing too great a readiness to believe things
credulous.definitionFr: crédule, naïf, trop enclin à croire n'importe quoi
sentences: Scam artists preyed upon credulous senior citizens by convincing them to send emergency wire transfers to protect nonexistent lottery winnings.
The credulous child believed every word of the ghost story, insisting that a monster was hiding quietly inside his bedroom closet.
credulous.mnemonic: Crédule : prêt à tout croire sans esprit critique.

deify.definition: to worship or regard someone or something as a god
deify.definitionFr: déifier, idolâtrer, vénérer comme un dieu
sentences: Ancient Roman citizens were expected to deify deceased emperors by erecting towering statues and performing sacred civic sacrifices in temples.
Music fans often deify rock legends, treating their everyday opinions as sacred revelations rather than ordinary artistic commentary on social life.
deify.mnemonic: Déifier : faire d'un mortel un dieu (deus en latin).

demystify.definition: to make a difficult subject clearer and easier to understand
sentences: The popular science podcast aimed to demystify quantum physics for curious high school students using everyday kitchen cooking analogies.
A good financial advisor should demystify retirement planning, explaining complex investment portfolios in straightforward terms that clients easily comprehend.
demystify.mnemonic: Démystifier : ôter le mystère pour rendre évident.

deride.definition: to express contempt for; to ridicule or mock
sentences: Skeptical theater critics derided the experimental play for its incomprehensible dialogue, yet avant-garde audiences applauded every provocative performance.
Colleagues initially derided her novel solar panel prototype as unworkable, but they apologized when it doubled energy conversion efficiency.
deride.mnemonic: Tourner en dérision : rire méchamment aux dépens de quelqu'un.

despot.definition: a ruler or other person who holds absolute, oppressive power
sentences: The cruel despot suppressed all political dissent, imprisoning independent journalists and banning public assemblies throughout the frightened nation.
Employees dreaded working for the corporate despot, who micromanaged every minor assignment and fired subordinates without legitimate justification or warning.
despot.mnemonic: Despote : souverain autoritaire qui n'admet aucune contestation.

diatribe.definition: a forceful and bitter verbal attack against someone or something
diatribe.definitionFr: diatribe, violente critique verbale ou écrite
sentences: The angry customer launched into a furious diatribe against the airline staff when his international flight was canceled without explanation.
In his fiery editorial, the journalist penned a scathing diatribe attacking municipal corruption and wasteful spending on unfinished sports stadiums.
diatribe.mnemonic: Diatribe : discours ou texte incendiaire qui attaque violemment.

dichotomy.definition: a division or contrast between two things that are opposed
dichotomy.definitionFr: dichotomie, division tranchée en deux contraires
sentences: The essay explores the false dichotomy between economic growth and environmental preservation, demonstrating that sustainable technologies promote both goals.
Philosophers frequently examine the sharp dichotomy between reason and emotion, debating which faculty should guide important moral life choices.
dichotomy.mnemonic: Dicho (en deux) + tomie (couper) : scinder nettement en deux parties opposées.

didactic.definition: intended to teach, particularly in having moral instruction as an ulterior motive
sentences: Although children enjoyed the colorful fairy tale illustrations, critics found the story overly didactic because of its heavy-handed moral lessons.
The museum exhibition adopted an engaging rather than didactic tone, inviting visitors to form their own interpretations of historical artifacts.
didactic.mnemonic: Didactique : qui vise à enseigner ou faire la leçon.

dilate.definition: to make or become wider, larger, or more open
sentences: The optometrist applied special medicated drops to dilate the patient's pupils before examining the sensitive retina for signs of disease.
When the frightened cat stepped into the dark hallway, its eyes began to dilate to capture every available ray of light.
dilate.mnemonic: Dilater : augmenter de volume ou s'élargir.

disaffected.definition: dissatisfied with authority, government, or a group and no longer loyal
sentences: The protest movement drew support from thousands of disaffected factory workers who felt abandoned by union leadership and political parties.
Disaffected young voters boycotted the election to protest widespread official corruption, refusing to endorse any established parliamentary candidate.
disaffected.mnemonic: Disaffected : qui a perdu son attachement ou son affection envers une institution.

disavow.definition: to deny any responsibility or support for something
sentences: The governor moved quickly to disavow the controversial remarks made by his campaign manager during an unsanctioned television interview yesterday.
Although the tech company funded the lobbyist, executives publicly disavowed his aggressive tactics once the scandal hit national newspaper headlines.
disavow.mnemonic: Désavouer : affirmer qu'on n'a rien à voir avec des actes blâmables.

disconcerting.definition: causing one to feel unsettled, confused, or embarrassed
sentences: The candidate found it disconcerting that the interviewer kept frowning silently at every answer without taking a single written note.
Hearing unexplained rhythmic tapping noises from the attic at midnight was a deeply disconcerting experience for the nervous new homeowner.
disconcerting.mnemonic: Déconcertant : qui fait perdre contenance ou déstabilise.

dissipation.definition: the squandering of money or resources; excessive indulgence in sensual pleasures
sentences: Years of reckless dissipation in European gambling casinos left the wealthy young heir completely destitute before his thirtieth birthday.
The physicist demonstrated the gradual dissipation of heat energy from the cooling engine into the chilly surrounding atmospheric air.
dissipation.mnemonic: Dissipation : dispersion des biens ou de l'énergie dans des plaisirs futiles.

divulge.definition: to make known private or sensitive information
sentences: Under strict corporate nondisclosure agreements, software developers are forbidden to divulge proprietary source code to rival tech firms.
The loyal butler refused to divulge any private details regarding the duchess's personal life despite persistent bribery attempts by eager reporters.
divulge.mnemonic: Divulguer : rendre public un secret qui devait rester caché.

doctrinaire.definition: seeking to impose a doctrine in all circumstances without regard to practical considerations
doctrinaire.definitionFr: doctrinaire, dogmatique, borné à une théorie rigide
sentences: The board rejected the doctrinaire economist whose rigid theoretical models failed to account for volatile shifts in consumer behavior.
Rather than adopting pragmatic solutions to the fiscal crisis, party leaders maintained a doctrinaire stance that alienated moderate coalition voters.
doctrinaire.mnemonic: Doctrinaire : enfermé dans sa doctrine sans regarder la réalité.

dogmatic.definition: inclined to lay down principles as incontrovertibly true
dogmatic.definitionFr: dogmatique, catégorique, intolérant à la contradiction
sentences: The professor was so dogmatic in his lectures that he dismissed any student question that challenged his chosen literary interpretations.
A good scientific researcher should remain open to unexpected experimental evidence instead of clinging to dogmatic beliefs about natural laws.
dogmatic.mnemonic: Dogmatique : assène des dogmes comme des vérités absolues.

dupe.definition: to deceive or trick someone easily
dupe.definitionFr: duper, tromper, abuser de la naïveté
sentences: The cunning con artist managed to dupe dozens of investors into funding an imaginary gold mine in South America.
Clever counterfeiters attempted to dupe the art museum curator by coating the fake canvas in antique varnish and artificial soot.
dupe.mnemonic: Duper : faire de quelqu'un une dupe (une victime crédule).

duplicitous.definition: deceitful and double-dealing in words or actions
duplicitous.definitionFr: fourbe, hypocrite, menteur à double visage
sentences: The duplicitous diplomat promised peace during press briefings while secretly coordinating military shipments to rebel forces across the border.
Colleagues avoided the duplicitous manager, who smiled pleasantly in meetings but routinely took personal credit for other team members' ideas.
duplicitous.mnemonic: Duplicitous : duplicité, le fait d'avoir deux visages (double jeu).

dynamism.definition: the quality of being characterized by vigorous activity and progress
sentences: The economic dynamism of the coastal technology hub attracted ambitious software developers, venture capital investors, and entrepreneurs from worldwide.
Critics praised the orchestral performance for its rhythmic dynamism, which infused the romantic symphony with fresh dramatic tension and passion.
dynamism.mnemonic: Dynamisme : force en mouvement, énergie qui propulse vers l'avant.

eclectic.definition: deriving ideas, style, or taste from a broad and diverse range of sources
eclectic.definitionFr: éclectique, varié, puisant dans des sources diverses
sentences: Her eclectic record collection ranged from classical baroque concertos and vintage Mississippi blues to modern electronic dance synthesizer tracks.
The chef developed an eclectic menu that fused traditional Japanese fermentation techniques with rustic French pastry traditions and Mexican spices.
eclectic.mnemonic: Éclectique : qui choisit le meilleur parmi des domaines très variés.

effectual.definition: successful in producing a desired result; effective
effectual.definitionFr: efficace, qui produit pleinement l'effet attendu
sentences: Diplomatic economic sanctions proved to be an effectual weapon, forcing the aggressive regime to halt its illicit uranium enrichment programs.
The municipal health committee introduced effectual hygiene measures that halted the cholera outbreak across crowded urban districts within two weeks.
effectual.mnemonic: Effectual = produit un effet certain, efficace.

egalitarian.definition: believing in or based on the principle that all people are equal
egalitarian.definitionFr: égalitaire, fondé sur l'égalité de tous
sentences: The progressive cooperative maintained an egalitarian workplace structure where all employees received equal compensation and voted on corporate decisions.
Sociologists praised the Scandinavian educational system for its egalitarian approach, which provided identical high-quality funding to every public neighborhood school.
egalitarian.mnemonic: Égalitaire : du français égal, qui vise l'égalité des droits et des chances.

elucidate.definition: to make something clear; to explain lucidly
sentences: The guest speaker used vivid diagrams to elucidate the complex mechanisms of cellular photosynthesis for the introductory biology students.
Historians examined newly declassified wartime diaries to elucidate the secret diplomatic negotiations that ultimately ended the Pacific conflict.
elucidate.mnemonic: Élucider : du latin lux (lumière), jeter de la lumière sur un mystère.

emulate.definition: to match or surpass a person or achievement, typically by imitation
emulate.definitionFr: émuler, imiter avec l'ambition d'égaler ou surpasser
sentences: Young pianists around the world strive to emulate the technical precision and emotional expressiveness of the legendary concert maestro.
Emerging startups often try to emulate the disruptive business model that propelled the ride-sharing company to international commercial success.
emulate.mnemonic: Émuler : rivaliser d'émulation, prendre modèle pour faire aussi bien.

engender.definition: to cause or give rise to a feeling, situation, or condition
sentences: The mayor's evasive answers during the televised press conference only served to engender deeper public mistrust in the municipal administration.
Creating an open classroom environment can engender lively intellectual debate and encourage shy students to share their creative perspectives freely.
engender.mnemonic: Engendrer : donner naissance à un sentiment ou une situation.

enigmatic.definition: difficult to interpret or understand; mysterious
sentences: Art historians have debated the enigmatic smile of the Mona Lisa for centuries without reaching a universally accepted consensus interpretation.
The detective studied the enigmatic clues left behind by the elusive cat burglar, hoping to anticipate his next nocturnal target.
enigmatic.mnemonic: Énigmatique : qui pose une énigme difficile à résoudre.

ephemeral.definition: lasting for a very short time; fleeting
ephemeral.definitionFr: éphémère, de très courte durée, fugace
sentences: The internet celebrity discovered that online fame is remarkably ephemeral, as fans quickly moved on to newer viral entertainment sensations.
Spring cherry blossoms offer an ephemeral beauty, gracing the mountain trees with delicate pink petals for only two brief weeks.
ephemeral.mnemonic: Éphémère : comme le papillon éphémère qui ne vit qu'un jour.

equivocal.definition: open to more than one interpretation; ambiguous or uncertain
sentences: The laboratory test results were frustratingly equivocal, neither confirming nor ruling out the presence of the rare autoimmune antibody condition.
Voters grew annoyed with the senator's equivocal replies on tax reform, demanding a direct yes or no answer instead.
equivocal.mnemonic: Équivoque : aequi (égal) + vox (voix) = susceptible de s'interpréter de deux manières.

erudite.definition: having or showing great knowledge or learning; scholarly
erudite.definitionFr: érudit, savant, doté d'une vaste culture
sentences: The erudite historian could recite ancient Greek philosophy from memory and contextualize medieval political treaties with impressive academic nuance.
Her erudite lecture on Renaissance literature impressed both distinguished university professors and visiting graduate students with its depth.
erudite.mnemonic: Érudit : personne dotée d'une immense culture livresque.

estimable.definition: worthy of great respect, admiration, or esteem
estimable.definitionFr: estimable, digne d'admiration et de respect
sentences: The retiring judge had compiled an estimable record of fair decisions and integrity throughout four decades on the federal court bench.
Despite fierce political differences, the prime minister recognized his late opponent as an estimable statesman of deep moral principle.
estimable.mnemonic: Estimable : qui mérite toute notre estime et notre considération.

euphemism.definition: a mild or indirect word used in place of an offensive or harsh one
euphemism.definitionFr: euphémisme, formulation adoucie pour atténuer une réalité brutale
sentences: The corporate human resources director used the euphemism workforce reduction to soften the painful reality of mass factory layoffs.
Saying that someone has passed away is a common euphemism used to discuss death without causing acute distress to grieving relatives.
euphemism.mnemonic: Euphémisme : eu (bien) + phémi (parler) = atténuer une vérité crue.

euphoria.definition: a feeling or state of intense excitement, happiness, and well-being
euphoria.definitionFr: euphorie, intense sentiment de bien-être et de joie
sentences: A wave of wild euphoria swept through the packed soccer stadium as the home team scored the winning goal in overtime.
Running the marathon produced a sudden surge of neurochemical euphoria that made the exhausted athlete forget all her muscular pain.
euphoria.mnemonic: Euphorie : état d'allégresse débordante et de bien-être absolu.

exodus.definition: a mass departure of people, especially from a difficult situation
sentences: The sudden outbreak of civil war triggered a tragic exodus of hundreds of thousands of refugees across the northern border.
Rising housing costs in the metropolitan area caused an exodus of young families toward more affordable rural towns each year.
exodus.mnemonic: Exode : ex (hors de) + hodos (chemin) = départ en masse.

exorbitant.definition: unreasonably high or excessive, especially of a price or demand
sentences: Tourists refused to pay the exorbitant prices charged by souvenir shops outside the cathedral, walking to local markets instead.
The landlord demanded an exorbitant rent increase that forced the beloved neighborhood bookstore to close after forty years of community service.
exorbitant.mnemonic: Exorbitant : ex-orbite, qui sort complètement des limites raisonnables.

exuberant.definition: filled with or characterized by a lively energy and enthusiasm
exuberant.definitionFr: exubérant, débordant d'énergie et de joie
sentences: The exuberant puppies bounded across the green lawn, barking happily and tumbling playfully over each other in the warm sunshine.
The crowd gave an exuberant cheer as their hometown Olympic athlete stepped proudly onto the podium to receive the gold medal.
exuberant.mnemonic: Exubérant : qui déborde d'enthousiasme et de vitalité.

faction.definition: a small organized dissenting group within a larger one
faction.definitionFr: faction, groupe dissident au sein d'une organisation
sentences: A militant faction broke away from the mainstream political party, refusing to endorse the moderate compromise negotiated by parliamentary leaders.
Bitter infighting between rival factions weakened the rebel movement and allowed government forces to recapture strategic mountain supply routes quickly.
faction.mnemonic: Faction : petit groupe querelleur qui divise un ensemble uni.

fallacious.definition: based on a mistaken belief or unsound reasoning
fallacious.definitionFr: fallacieux, trompeur, fondé sur un faux raisonnement
sentences: The defense lawyer exposed the fallacious logic in the prosecutor's closing argument, pointing out glaring contradictions in the witness testimony.
Believing that high correlation automatically implies direct causation is a classic fallacious assumption frequently made by novice data science researchers.
fallacious.mnemonic: Fallacieux : du latin fallere (tromper), qui induit en erreur par un sophisme.

fervent.definition: having or displaying a passionate intensity
fervent.definitionFr: fervent, passionné, ardent dans ses convictions
sentences: As a fervent environmental activist, she spent every weekend organizing beach cleanups and petitioning lawmakers to protect coastal wildlife preserves.
The congregation offered a fervent prayer for peace and safety during the tense days following the disastrous regional earthquake strike.
fervent.mnemonic: Fervent : brûlant d'ardeur et de conviction sincère.

frank.definition: open, honest, and direct in speech or writing
frank.definitionFr: franc, direct, sans détour ni faux-semblant
sentences: The mentor had a frank conversation with the struggling student, clearly outlining his academic deficiencies while encouraging him to persist.
Her frank review of the overrated novel upset the author, but readers appreciated her refreshing honesty about its weak plotting.
frank.mnemonic: Franc : parler sans fard ni déguisement, droit au but.

galvanize.definition: to shock or excite someone into taking action
galvanize.definitionFr: galvaniser, électriser, inciter fortement à l'action
sentences: The activist's impassioned speech helped galvanize thousands of ordinary citizens into protesting against deep public school funding budget cuts.
The shocking investigative report served to galvanize regulatory authorities into launching immediate inspections of offshore oil drilling operations nationwide.
galvanize.mnemonic: Galvaniser : de Galvani (électricité), comme recevoir une décharge qui réveille.

grandiose.definition: impressive or magnificent in appearance or style, especially pretentiously so
