Decades of geological data offered incontrovertible evidence that the ancient tectonic plates had shifted gradually over millions of tumultuous years.
incontrovertible.mnemonic: In-controvertible : contre lequel on ne peut soulever aucune controverse.

indemnify.definition: to compensate for harm or loss; secure against legal responsibility
sentences: The insurance policy promised to indemnify the homeowner against any flood damage caused by severe hurricanes during the autumn season.
The construction contract required the developer to indemnify the city against potential lawsuits resulting from workplace accidents on site.
indemnify.mnemonic: Indemniser en français : dédommager une personne pour une perte subie.

intelligible.definition: able to be understood; clear and comprehensible
sentences: The professor managed to make quantum mechanics intelligible to undergraduate students by using simple analogies drawn from everyday life.
Although the radio transmission was filled with static, the pilot's distress call remained intelligible enough for air traffic control to respond.
intelligible.mnemonic: Intelligible : qui peut être compris par l'intellect sans difficulté.

inveterate.definition: having a long-established habit or interest that is unlikely to change
sentences: An inveterate gambler, he spent every Friday evening at the downtown poker tables, ignoring the sensible warnings of his worried family.
Even after retiring from journalism, the inveterate writer continued waking up at dawn to draft opinion columns about national political developments.
inveterate.mnemonic: Invétéré : enraciné avec l'âge (du latin vetus, vieux).

irascible.definition: having a tendency to be easily angered; irritable
sentences: The irascible chef threw a copper pot across the kitchen whenever an assistant made even the slightest mistake with a sauce.
Exhausted by the noisy construction outside his window, the elderly tenant became increasingly irascible, shouting at anyone who knocked on his door.
irascible.mnemonic: Irascible : qui cède facilement à l'ire (la colère).

irony.definition: a state of affairs or event contrary to what was expected
sentences: The tragic irony of the inventor's life was that the safety device he created ultimately caused the fatal carriage accident that killed him.
Nobody missed the irony when the climate conference delegates arrived at the summit aboard hundreds of private, carbon-spewing corporate jets.
irony.mnemonic: L'ironie d'une situation où le résultat contredit l'intention initiale.

kinetic.definition: relating to or resulting from motion; active and dynamic
sentences: The roller coaster converts kinetic energy into potential energy as the heavy cars climb steeply up the towering wooden track.
Critics praised the kinetic choreography of the modern dance troupe, whose relentless leaping captivated the audience throughout the two-hour performance.
kinetic.mnemonic: Cinétique en physique : lié au mouvement (du grec kinēsis).

laconic.definition: using very few words; concise and terse
sentences: The general was famous for his laconic dispatches from the front lines, often summarizing complex battles in just two brief sentences.
When asked if he intended to seek another term in office, the mayor offered only a laconic reply of no comment.
laconic.mnemonic: Comme les Spartiates de Laconie, réputés pour parler en très peu de mots.

languid.definition: lacking energy or vitality; pleasantly slow and relaxed
sentences: The oppressive summer heat made the tourists feel languid, so they spent the afternoon sipping iced tea beneath swaying palm trees.
With a languid wave of her hand, the aristocrat dismissed the servant and drifted off to sleep on the plush sofa.
languid.mnemonic: Languide : sans force ni entrain, qui se laisse aller à l'inaction.

languorous.definition: characterized by pleasant tiredness, dreamy languor, or relaxation
sentences: The couple enjoyed a languorous afternoon floating on the sunlit Mediterranean waters, completely unconcerned with schedules or mundane obligations.
Warm breezes and fragrant blossoms induced a languorous mood that kept the vacationers lounging by the pool for hours on end.
languorous.mnemonic: Langoureux : une paresse douce, sensuelle et pleine de volupté.

libertine.definition: a person who behaves without moral principles, especially sexually
sentences: The young libertine squandered his vast family fortune on lavish parties, heavy gambling, and endless affairs across the capitals of Europe.
In the satirical play, the charming libertine seduces several wealthy heiresses before his deceitful schemes are finally exposed in the final act.
libertine.mnemonic: Un libertin s'affranchit des règles morales pour jouir des plaisirs.

limpid.definition: completely clear and transparent; easily intelligible and lucid
sentences: The mountain stream was so limpid that hikers could clearly see smooth pebbles resting on the riverbed ten feet below.
Scholars praised the philosopher's limpid prose, which explained complex metaphysical concepts without resorting to obscure terminology or tangled syntax.
limpid.mnemonic: Limpide : clair et pur comme une eau de source cristalline.

loquacious.definition: tending to talk a great deal; extremely talkative
sentences: The loquacious barber kept chatting enthusiastically about neighborhood politics throughout the haircut, barely pausing to let his customer speak.
Dinner with the loquacious diplomat was always entertaining, though guests rarely managed to utter a word during his lengthy anecdotes.
loquacious.mnemonic: Loquace vient du latin loqui (parler) : qui parle avec abondance.

lugubrious.definition: looking or sounding mournful, dismal, or excessively gloomy
sentences: The cellist played a lugubrious melody that echoed through the quiet stone chapel, bringing several mourners in the pews to tears.
His lugubrious expression at the wedding reception made people wonder whether he was actually celebrating or mourning a profound personal tragedy.
lugubrious.mnemonic: Lugubre : d'une tristesse sombre et funèbre qui glace l'atmosphère.

machination.definition: a crafty scheme or plot designed to achieve an evil end
sentences: The ruthless advisor used every political machination at his disposal to undermine the prime minister and seize control of the cabinet.
Fortunately, the vigilant royal guards uncovered the conspirators' secret machination before they could carry out their treasonous plan against the king.
machination.mnemonic: Une machination : un complot ourdi dans l'ombre avec ruse.

mercenary.definition: primarily motivated by money or material gain; venal
sentences: The critic condemned the director's mercenary motives, arguing that the sequel was made solely to cash in on holiday merchandise sales.
Her mercenary suitors showed intense interest only after discovering she stood to inherit a massive real estate empire from her grandfather.
mercenary.mnemonic: Mercenaire : qui n'agit que pour l'appât du gain financier.

misanthrope.definition: a person who dislikes humankind and avoids human society
sentences: Living alone in a remote mountain cabin, the aging misanthrope posted trespass warnings to keep curious hikers far away from his doorstep.
Disillusioned by corporate corruption and political greed, he gradually turned into a bitter misanthrope who preferred the companionship of stray dogs.
misanthrope.mnemonic: Misanthrope : misos (haine) + anthropos (humain) = ennemi du genre humain.

mordant.definition: sharply or bitingly sarcastic; caustic in tone
sentences: The satirist was famous for her mordant humor, which regularly mocked pompous politicians and exposed the absurdities of modern consumer culture.
His mordant review of the new restaurant criticized the soggy pasta and dismissed the dessert menu as culinary malpractice in print.
mordant.mnemonic: Mordant : un humour si acéré qu'il semble mordre la victime.

myopic.definition: lacking foresight or intellectual insight; narrow-minded and shortsighted
sentences: Environmentalists criticized the government's myopic policy of draining wetlands for shopping malls, which caused severe flooding in later years.
The executive's myopic focus on immediate quarterly profits led him to cut research spending, ultimately crippling the company's long-term innovation.
myopic.mnemonic: Myope au figuré : incapable de regarder au-delà du court terme.

nadir.definition: the lowest or most unsuccessful point in a situation
sentences: The economic depression marked the nadir of the manufacturer's fortunes, as sales plunged and factories were forced to shut down nationwide.
After losing his job and his apartment in the same week, he felt he had reached the emotional nadir of his life.
nadir.mnemonic: Le nadir est à l'opposé du zénith : le point le plus bas possible.

nebulous.definition: vague, indistinct, or ill-defined; cloudy in shape
sentences: The candidate offered only nebulous promises about improving healthcare, failing to explain how her costly proposals would actually be funded.
Before the invention of telescopes, astronomers held nebulous ideas about distant galaxies, assuming they were merely glowing clouds of interstellar dust.
nebulous.mnemonic: Nébuleux vient de nebula (nuage) : flou et difficile à cerner.

neophyte.definition: a person who is new to a subject or activity; novice
sentences: Although she was a neophyte in computer programming, her rapid grasp of algorithms astonished the senior software engineers at the startup.
The experienced climbing instructor patiently guided the terrified neophyte through the basic knot-tying exercises before tackling the sheer rock face.
neophyte.mnemonic: Néo (nouveau) + phyte (planté) : nouveau venu dans un groupe ou domaine.

nutritive.definition: providing nourishment; nutritious and sustaining to life
sentences: Dietitians recommend legumes because their high nutritive value provides essential proteins, dietary fibers, and minerals needed for a healthy lifestyle.
The remote islanders relied on coconut palms as their primary nutritive source, harvesting the fruits for both food and fresh drinking water.
nutritive.mnemonic: Nutritif : qui apporte à l'organisme tous les nutriments nécessaires.

obsequious.definition: obedient or attentive to an excessive or servile degree
sentences: The obsequious assistant flattered the CEO constantly and laughed loudly at his dullest jokes in hopes of securing a quick promotion.
Waiters at the exclusive club were trained to be attentive without appearing obsequious, balancing refined professionalism with polite customer discretion.
obsequious.mnemonic: Obséquieux : politesse exagérée et rampante pour s'attirer des faveurs.

oeuvre.definition: the complete body of work of an artist, writer, or composer
sentences: The retrospective exhibition celebrated the entire oeuvre of the sculptor, tracing her evolution from classical marble statues to modern abstract installations.
Literary historians consider the tragic trilogy the crowning achievement of the playwright's oeuvre, cementing his reputation as an enduring master.
oeuvre.mnemonic: L'œuvre complète d'un artiste, emprunté tel quel au français en anglais.

opprobrium.definition: harsh criticism or censure; public disgrace from shameful conduct
sentences: The disgraced politician faced widespread public opprobrium after leaked audio recordings exposed his secret involvement in the bribery scandal.
Athletes caught using performance-enhancing drugs suffer lasting opprobrium, losing lucrative sponsorships and seeing their past championship titles permanently revoked.
opprobrium.mnemonic: Jeter l'opprobre sur quelqu'un : le couvrir d'une honte méritée.

ostentatious.definition: characterized by vulgar or pretentious display designed to impress
sentences: The billionaire built an ostentatious mansion with gold-plated fountains and marble columns that drew disdainful sneers from his more modest neighbors.
Rather than wearing an ostentatious diamond necklace to the charity gala, she chose an elegant silver bracelet that complemented her dress.
ostentatious.mnemonic: Ostentatoire : qui fait étalage de son luxe de façon tapageuse.

panacea.definition: a solution or remedy for all difficulties or diseases
sentences: The economist warned that deregulation was not a panacea for the nation's financial crisis, as structural poverty required multifaceted government intervention.
Early patent medicine vendors hawked tonic bottles as a magical panacea capable of curing everything from common colds to chronic arthritis.
panacea.mnemonic: Panacée : pan (tout) + akos (remède), le remède universel illusoire.

panache.definition: flamboyant confidence of style or manner; stylish flair
sentences: The maestro conducted the final movement with extraordinary panache, sweeping his baton through the air with dazzling dramatic flourishes.
Even while facing intense questioning from reporters, the diplomat handled every hostile inquiry with enviable panache and disarming wit.
panache.mnemonic: Avoir du panache : fierté éclatante et allure brillante (comme Cyrano).

paradigm.definition: a typical example, pattern, or framework of something
sentences: The introduction of the internet created a new paradigm for business, forcing traditional retail stores to adapt to digital commerce rapidly.
In scientific revolutions, an established paradigm often resists replacement until mounting contradictory evidence makes its core assumptions completely untenable.
paradigm.mnemonic: Un paradigme : le cadre théorique ou modèle de référence dominant.

paragon.definition: a person or thing regarded as a model of excellence
sentences: Revered as a paragon of journalistic integrity, the veteran editor refused to publish sensational rumors without verifying every supporting document.
The academy held up the young scholar as a paragon of intellectual discipline, praising her tireless research and brilliant philosophical treatises.
paragon.mnemonic: Un parangon de vertu : modèle idéal réunissant toutes les qualités.

parsimonious.definition: unwilling to spend money or use resources; excessively frugal
sentences: The parsimonious landlord refused to replace the broken furnace during winter, forcing freezing tenants to buy their own electric space heaters.
Despite his immense personal fortune, the parsimonious billionaire drove a rusted compact car and always reused old paper tea bags.
parsimonious.mnemonic: Parcimonieux : qui donne au compte-gouttes par avarice.

pastiche.definition: an artistic work in a style that imitates another artist
sentences: The author's latest detective novel is a clever pastiche of Victorian mystery fiction, complete with foggy London alleys and eccentric inspectors.
Critics dismissed the director's new movie as an uninspired pastiche of classic film noir tropes rather than an original cinematic vision.
pastiche.mnemonic: Un pastiche : œuvre d'art qui reproduit délibérément le style d'un maître.

patronage.definition: financial support or sponsorship given by a patron to artists
sentences: During the Renaissance, generous royal patronage enabled painters and architects to produce timeless masterpieces that transformed European cultural heritage.
Without the continuous patronage of wealthy benefactors, the struggling regional opera company would have been forced to cancel its winter season.
patronage.mnemonic: Le mécénat ou patronage assure aux créateurs les ressources pour travailler.

peccadillo.definition: a small, relatively unimportant offense, sin, or fault
sentences: The candidate hoped voters would forgive his youthful peccadillo, arguing that stealing a campus street sign was merely an immature college prank.
While a forgotten anniversary might seem like a minor peccadillo, it ignited a week of bitter arguments between the stressed spouses.
peccadillo.mnemonic: Une peccadille : péché véniel (peccatum), péché mignon sans gravité.

perfidious.definition: deceitful and untrustworthy; treacherous in violation of trust
sentences: The perfidious ally secretly negotiated a peace treaty with the enemy while our soldiers were still fighting in the distant trenches.
Historians condemned the general's perfidious conduct, noting that he accepted bribes from foreign emissaries to surrender the fortified citadel without resistance.
perfidious.mnemonic: Perfide : per + fides (foi), qui trahit sa parole et rompt la confiance.

pernicious.definition: having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or insidious way
sentences: Unchecked misinformation on social media has a pernicious influence on public health, convincing thousands of vulnerable people to reject proven vaccines.
The doctor warned that stress causes pernicious damage to the cardiovascular system over time, often progressing silently before symptoms suddenly emerge.
pernicious.mnemonic: Pernicieux : un mal discret et pervers qui ruine tout de l'intérieur.

philistine.definition: a person who is hostile or indifferent to culture and arts
sentences: The philistine complained loudly throughout the museum tour, declaring that modern abstract sculptures looked like heaps of twisted scrap metal.
When the council slashed funding for the local library, angry residents accused the mayor of being a philistine who despised literature.
philistine.mnemonic: Philistin : insensible aux arts et aux raffinements de l'esprit.

phlegmatic.definition: having an unemotional, calm, and stolid disposition
sentences: The phlegmatic pilot remained completely calm when the plane's starboard engine failed, safely landing the aircraft without causing any passenger panic.
Even during fierce political debates, her phlegmatic demeanor never cracked, allowing her to deliver rational rebuttals while her opponents lost control.
phlegmatic.mnemonic: Flegmatique : sang-froid imperturbable en toute circonstance.

polemic.definition: a strong verbal or written attack on someone or something
sentences: The philosopher published a fiery polemic against modern consumer capitalism, condemning the mindless obsession with wealth that alienated urban workers.
Rather than offering a balanced historical review, the book read like an angry polemic aimed at destroying the former premier's legacy.
polemic.mnemonic: Polémique : polémos (guerre), combat d'idées véhément et passionné.

prescient.definition: having or showing knowledge of events before they take place
sentences: The economist's prescient warnings about the housing bubble were initially dismissed by bank executives who later faced catastrophic financial collapses.
Reading the author's prescient novel fifty years after its publication is chilling, as it accurately predicted artificial intelligence and pervasive surveillance.
prescient.mnemonic: Pré-scient : prae (avant) + scire (savoir), qui prévoit l'avenir.

probity.definition: the quality of having strong moral principles; honesty and integrity
sentences: The judge was renowned for her unwavering probity, strictly refusing campaign donations and recusing herself whenever personal interests were involved.
Financial regulators commended the bank's strict probity, noting that its audits consistently complied with the highest ethical standards of accounting.
probity.mnemonic: La probité : l'intégrité morale irréprochable et incorruptible.

progenitor.definition: an ancestor, parent, or originator of an artistic movement
sentences: Geneticists traced the rare hereditary mutation back to a single progenitor who lived in northern Scandinavia during the fourteenth century.
Critics regard Edgar Allan Poe as the progenitor of modern detective fiction, noting that his Dupin stories inspired Arthur Conan Doyle.
progenitor.mnemonic: Pro-géniteur : l'ancêtre fondateur qui engendre une lignée ou école.

prognostication.definition: the action of prophesying future events; a forecast
sentences: Despite the gloomy prognostication of weather forecasters, the dark storm clouds dispersed by noon, allowing the outdoor festival to proceed.
Market analysts issued a dire prognostication regarding tech stocks, anticipating a severe market correction before the end of the fiscal quarter.
prognostication.mnemonic: Prognostication / pronostic : prévision établie d'après des signes.

prolix.definition: using or containing too many words; tediously wordy and long-winded
sentences: The lawyer's prolix brief annoyed the busy judge, who demanded a concise summary instead of fifty pages of repetitive legal jargon.
His prolix speech dragged on for nearly three hours, causing tired audience members to check their watches and quietly leave the auditorium.
prolix.mnemonic: Prolixe : qui se perd dans un déluge de mots inutiles.

promulgate.definition: to promote or make widely known; put a law into effect
sentences: The emperor issued a royal decree to promulgate religious tolerance throughout his vast domains, forbidding local magistrates from persecuting minorities.
Health agencies worked together to promulgate essential hygiene guidelines, using radio and television to reach rural villages during the epidemic.
promulgate.mnemonic: Promulguer : proclamer officiellement une loi pour qu'elle prenne effet.

propitious.definition: giving or indicating a good chance of success; favorable and auspicious
sentences: The calm sea and steady morning breeze created propitious conditions for the sailing crew to set out on their transoceanic voyage.
Economists agreed that low interest rates and booming consumer confidence made this a propitious moment for entrepreneurs to launch new businesses.
propitious.mnemonic: Propice : qui offre des conditions favorables à la réussite.

prosaic.definition: having the style of prose; lacking poetic beauty; ordinary and commonplace
sentences: While she dreamed of exciting adventures in exotic lands, her daily life consisted of prosaic chores like filing invoices and answering emails.
The architect transformed what could have been a prosaic concrete office building into an inspiring work of art with soaring glass atriums.
prosaic.mnemonic: Prosaïque : terre à terre comme de la simple prose, sans poésie.

proscribe.definition: to forbid, especially by law; denounce or outlaw formally
sentences: The new environmental regulations proscribe the dumping of industrial toxic chemicals into public waterways, imposing hefty fines on violating factories.
Authoritarian regimes routinely proscribe independent newspapers and arrest dissenting reporters to maintain tight control over the flow of public information.

provident.definition: making or indicating timely preparation for the future; prudent and thrifty
sentences: Thanks to her provident habits of saving half her paycheck every month, she weathered the unexpected job loss without accumulating debt.
The provident farmers stored surplus wheat in dry silos during bountiful years to ensure their village would survive potential future droughts.
provident.mnemonic: Prévoyant : qui pourvoit d'avance (provide) aux besoins à venir.

puerile.definition: childishly silly and trivial; immature and foolish
sentences: The CEO was infuriated by the puerile pranks played by the interns, warning them that hiding office chairs was completely unprofessional.
Rather than presenting mature policy arguments, the debate deteriorated into puerile name-calling that embarrassed both political parties on national television.
puerile.mnemonic: Puéril vient du latin puer (enfant) : comportement bêtement gamin.

pugnacious.definition: eager or quick to argue, quarrel, or fight; combative
sentences: The pugnacious hockey player spent half the championship game inside the penalty box for picking fights with the opposing team's defenseman.
Known for his pugnacious interview style, the aggressive journalist constantly interrupted politicians whenever they attempted to dodge difficult budgetary questions.
pugnacious.mnemonic: Pugnace vient de pugnus (poing) : toujours prêt à en découdre.

quotidian.definition: of or occurring every day; daily and ordinary
sentences: The painter found profound beauty in the quotidian routines of domestic life, depicting scenes of women baking bread and sweeping sunlit porches.
Escaping from the quotidian grind of commuting and desk work, the backpackers spent two glorious weeks hiking in the Canadian wilderness.
quotidian.mnemonic: Quotidien : ce qui revient chaque jour et fait la banalité ordinaire.

raconteur.definition: a person who tells anecdotes in a skillful and amusing way
sentences: A gifted raconteur, my grandfather held the dinner guests spellbound with humorous stories about his youthful adventures across South America.
The beloved tavern owner was a natural raconteur whose captivating ghost legends drew curious tourists from neighboring towns every autumn evening.
raconteur.mnemonic: Raconteur : emprunt direct au français pour désigner un as de la narration.

rapacious.definition: aggressively greedy or grasping; predatory in taking what belongs to others
sentences: The rapacious corporation bought out struggling family farms and drastically slashed worker pensions to maximize returns for aggressive private equity investors.
Local fishermen condemned the rapacious trawlers that swept the seabed with giant nets, destroying delicate coral reefs and depleting regional fish stocks.
rapacious.mnemonic: Rapace : avide de butin comme un oiseau de proie affamé.

recalcitrant.definition: having an obstinately uncooperative attitude toward authority or discipline
sentences: The recalcitrant teenager refused to complete his homework assignments, defiantly crossing his arms whenever the teacher asked for his notebook.
Ranchers struggled for hours to guide the recalcitrant bull into the wooden trailer, as the stubborn animal refused to budge an inch.
recalcitrant.mnemonic: Récalcitrant : qui donne des ruades (recalcitrare), rebelle à l'autorité.

rectitude.definition: morally correct behavior or thinking; righteousness and probity
sentences: The public admired the former president for his impeccable moral rectitude, contrasting his honest leadership with the rampant corruption of successors.
Known for her intellectual rectitude, the research scientist withdrew her paper immediately upon discovering a flaw in her statistical calculations.
rectitude.mnemonic: Rectitude : marcher tout droit (rectus) sur le chemin du devoir.

relegate.definition: to assign an inferior rank, position, or status to someone
sentences: After losing five matches in a row, the famous football club was relegated to the second division for the next season.
The autocratic director tended to relegate dissenting board members to obscure committees where their critical opinions could exert no practical influence.
relegate.mnemonic: Reléguer : renvoyer à une position subalterne ou dans l'ombre.

repudiate.definition: to refuse to accept, recognize, or be associated with; reject
sentences: The prime minister felt compelled to repudiate the radical statements made by his defense minister, issuing a formal retraction to Parliament.
When new genetic evidence proved the prisoner's innocence, the appellate court moved swiftly to repudiate the flawed guilty verdict from years earlier.
repudiate.mnemonic: Répudier : rejeter formellement ce qu'on approuvait ou possédait jadis.

sage.definition: a profoundly wise person, especially one famed for sound judgment
sentences: Pilgrims traveled hundreds of miles across rugged mountain passes to seek advice from the ancient sage who dwelled in the quiet monastery.
Regarded as a political sage, the retired diplomat frequently advised world leaders on navigating complex multilateral treaties during international disputes.
sage.mnemonic: Un sage : homme vénérable dont l'expérience et la raison éclairent autrui.

salutary.definition: producing good effects; beneficial, especially despite being unwelcome
sentences: The painful audit served as a salutary lesson for the company, forcing executives to adopt far more rigorous accounting controls going forward.
Taking a brisk morning walk through the pine forest had a salutary effect on her health, relieving both physical stress and anxiety.
salutary.mnemonic: Salutaire : qui apporte un bénéfice ou un enseignement salvateur.

savant.definition: a learned person, especially a distinguished scientist or eminent scholar
sentences: The visiting savant delivered an extraordinary lecture on astrophysics, answering complex questions from university professors with effortless mastery and profound clarity.
Although socially awkward in large crowds, the mathematical savant could calculate prime numbers into the millions entirely within his head.
savant.mnemonic: Un savant : personne possédant une érudition profonde et reconnue.

seismic.definition: of enormous proportions or impact; relating to earthquakes
sentences: The fall of the Berlin Wall caused a seismic geopolitical shift across Eastern Europe, dismantling Soviet control within a few dramatic months.
The sudden merger of the two banking titans sent seismic shockwaves through financial markets, wiping out smaller brokerage firms within days.
seismic.mnemonic: Sismique : séisme en grec, qui ébranle les fondations mêmes de la société.

sententious.definition: given to moralizing in a pompous or affected manner
sentences: His sententious speech about the virtues of hard work fell flat on employees who had not received a pay raise in years.
Annoyed by her uncle's sententious sermons during Sunday dinners, the young student made an excuse to leave the dining table early.
sententious.mnemonic: Sentencieux : qui assène des sentences morales avec gravité prétentieuse.

serpentine.definition: winding and twisting like a snake; complex and cunning
sentences: The bus crawled carefully along the serpentine mountain road, where each sharp hairpin turn revealed a dizzying view of the gorge below.
Investigators spent months untangling the firm's serpentine corporate structure, which hid offshore bank accounts behind dozens of fraudulent dummy companies.
serpentine.mnemonic: Serpentin : qui ondule en courbes sinueuses à la façon d'un serpent.

sophistic.definition: plausible but fallacious; based on deceptive or specious reasoning
sentences: The debater relied on sophistic arguments to mislead the audience, twisting statistical definitions while ignoring the overwhelming scientific consensus on the topic.
The judge rejected the lawyer's sophistic reasoning, emphasizing that clever wordplay could not justify violating the explicit constitutional text of the statute.
sophistic.mnemonic: Sophistique : digne des sophistes, raisonnement faux sous des dehors séduisants.

soporific.definition: tending to induce drowsiness or sleep; tediously monotonous
sentences: The monotone voice of the substitute lecturer had a soporific effect on the crowded lecture hall, sending half the students to sleep.
Sipping warm chamomile tea while listening to gentle rain proved wonderfully soporific, helping the insomniac drift off after hours of restless tossing.
soporific.mnemonic: Soporifique vient de sopor (sommeil lourd) : qui donne irrésistiblement envie de dormir.

taciturn.definition: reserved or uncommunicative in speech; saying very little
sentences: The taciturn blacksmith rarely spoke more than three words to customers, preferring to let the rhythmic clanging of his hammer do the talking.
Although her husband was quite taciturn at social gatherings, he was remarkably warm and talkative when relaxing at home with his children.
taciturn.mnemonic: Taciturne : du latin tacere (taire), naturellement avare de paroles.

tendentious.definition: expressing or promoting a particular controversial point of view; biased
sentences: The editorial was criticized for its tendentious coverage of the election, as it highlighted the incumbent's minor achievements while ignoring corruption scandals.
Historians questioned the documentary's tendentious narrative, arguing that the filmmaker cherry-picked archival letters to support a predetermined conspiracy theory.
tendentious.mnemonic: Tendancieux : qui manifeste une intention partisane et déforme la vérité.

timorous.definition: showing or suffering from nervousness, fear, or lack of confidence
sentences: The timorous fawn stood frozen at the forest edge, darting back into the thick bushes at the slightest snap of a twig.
Because he was inherently timorous in confrontations, the junior associate avoided raising objections when the aggressive partner misstated key contractual clauses.
timorous.mnemonic: Timoré vient du latin timor (la peur) : trop craintif pour oser agir.

torpor.definition: a state of physical or mental inactivity; lethargy
sentences: After eating a heavy Thanksgiving dinner, the entire family sank into a pleasant torpor, dozing peacefully in front of the flickering television.
During the coldest weeks of winter, the hibernating bear remains in a deep torpor, conserving energy until warmer temperatures return in spring.
torpor.mnemonic: La torpeur : état d'engourdissement physique ou d'inertie mentale totale.

ubiquitous.definition: present, appearing, or found everywhere; omnipresent
sentences: Smartphones have become so ubiquitous in modern society that it is nearly impossible to spot a pedestrian walking without a screen in hand.
Once a rare luxury found only in high-end bakeries, artisanal coffee shops are now ubiquitous across almost every urban neighborhood in the country.
ubiquitous.mnemonic: L'ubiquité est la capacité d'être partout à la fois.

venal.definition: motivated by susceptibility to bribery; corrupt and open to bribery
sentences: The venal border inspector regularly accepted cash bribes from smugglers, looking the other way as contraband trucks crossed the checkpoint every night.
Outraged citizens demanded the resignation of the venal mayor after prosecutors revealed that municipal building contracts were routinely awarded to political donors.
venal.mnemonic: Vénal : qui se vend (du latin venire, être vendu) pour de l'argent.

verve.definition: vigor, spirit, or enthusiasm in artistic work or performance
sentences: The young violinist tackled the demanding concerto with astonishing verve, earning a standing ovation from the usually reserved subscription audience.
Readers admired the verve of the young novelist's debut, praising its lively dialogue and relentless narrative momentum from the very first chapter.
verve.mnemonic: Avoir de la verve : éclat, vivacité et brio dans l'expression artistique.

vituperation.definition: bitter and abusive language or condemnation; vitriol
sentences: The controversial referee was subjected to relentless vituperation from furious soccer fans after disallowing what appeared to be a perfectly valid goal.
Exhausted by the bitter vituperation exchanged on social media, the journalist decided to delete her account and focus entirely on print reporting.
vituperation.mnemonic: Vitupérer / vitupération : accabler d'invectives violentes et méprisantes.
